headline: I have successfully negotiated a formal rental lease for the space under my office desk to save on commuting costs
body:
It started as a simple cost-cutting measure when my daily commute from the suburbs began exceeding the length of a feature-length film. Last month, I approached my HR manager with a bold proposal: instead of paying 40,000 rupees for a studio apartment I only visit to sleep in, I would pay 12,000 rupees to officially 'occupy' the 4x3 foot crawlspace beneath my workstation. 

My desk-nest is surprisingly efficient. I have installed a memory-foam mat, a privacy curtain made of stacked copier paper boxes, and a portable steamer that allows me to prepare instant noodles using the office water cooler. The proximity to my laptop means I am officially the first person in the office every morning, which has earned me a 'Top Performer' badge and a significant bump in my annual bonus.

Sure, the janitorial staff occasionally sweeps around my sleeping bag during the midnight shift, but that’s a small price to pay for a forty-minute extension to my REM cycle. I have even managed to negotiate a secondary agreement for shared access to the server room for a monthly subscription fee, giving me a temperature-controlled walk-in closet. Why struggle with the local train during rush hour when your bed is already equipped with high-speed Wi-Fi and ergonomic cable management?
caption: Living the corporate dream, literally. Who needs a house when you have under-desk storage? #OfficeLife #RealEstate #UrbanLiving #WorkLifeBalance (satire)
